problems.text: Meeting requests arrive as free-form emailed text and the team manually parses each one into the system, taking 2 hours per request
Customers wait 24-48 hours for confirmation of a request
Risk: if the AI misparses a constraint, the meeting gets scheduled wrong

proposed_solutions.text: Parse the free-form requests into structured scheduling constraints; the Engineer Lead calls this NLU work
Automate 80% of the parsing with an LLM-based parser
Architecture proposed by the Engineer Lead: a fine-tuned model on the request data, a confidence threshold so low-confidence parses get human review, and monthly retraining on new labeled data

user_segments.text: One of the largest customers, a legal firm with complex scheduling rules
Other customers whose requests are also in the logs
The internal team that parses requests by hand

requests.text: Every parsed request still goes to a human for review; the AI output is a draft, not final
Measure parser accuracy on a holdout set
Monitor drift over time as request patterns evolve
Ongoing evals and retraining; this is not a one-time model

action_items.text: Spec the architecture, as proposed by the Engineer Lead

metrics_mentioned.text: One large customer sent 500 meeting requests last month
The team spends 2 hours per request on manual parsing
For 500 requests, the VP Product says that is 1000 hours per month of manual work
Logs of those 500 requests plus another 800 from other customers: 1300 labeled examples of free-form request to structured output
Customers currently wait 24-48 hours for confirmation; with automation the Customer Success Manager says it could be minutes
Data Analyst: an MVP could be running in 4 weeks
